title: Στο ταξί
brief: You've just landed in Athens. You're outside the terminal with a suitcase, and a taxi driver is looking at you.

visit.brief: Get yourself and your suitcase to the Hotel Akropoli, and find out what it costs.
visit.summary: Took a taxi from the airport to the hotel; the driver was friendly and it cost twenty euros.
visit.translation:
— Good evening! Taxi?
— Good evening. Yes, please. I'd like to go to the Hotel Akropoli.
— Okay. Is this your suitcase?
— Yes, thank you. Is it far?
— No, twenty minutes. Where are you from?
— From America. Do you speak English?
— A little. You speak Greek!
— A little Greek. How much is it?
— Twenty euros.
— Here you are. Thank you very much!
— You're welcome. Enjoy your stay!

prompts.situation: You're in the taxi. Tell the driver, politely, that you'd like to go to the Hotel Akropoli.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Θα ήθελα να πάω στο ξενοδοχείο Ακρόπολη, παρακαλώ.

prompts.situation: The ride is over. Ask how much it is.

title: Στο καφέ
brief: A café on a square, 9am, already warm. The waiter comes over with a notepad.

visit.brief: Order a coffee the Greek way, say how you take it, and ask for the bill.
visit.summary: Ordered an iced coffee with a little sugar and a water; the bill was three euros.
visit.translation:
— Good morning! What will you have?
— Good morning. A coffee, please. And a water.
— Hot or cold, the coffee?
— Cold, please. A frappé.
— With sugar? With milk?
— With a little sugar, no milk.
— Okay. Anything else?
— No, thank you. That's all.
— Here you are, your coffee and the water.
— Thank you very much. The bill, please.
— Three euros.

bundle.gloss: The object changes: ο → τον, η → την

prompts.situation: The waiter asks what you'll have. Order a coffee and a water.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Έναν καφέ, παρακαλώ. Και ένα νερό.

prompts.situation: You're done. Ask for the bill.

title: Στην ταβέρνα
brief: A seaside taverna at dusk, paper tablecloths, a cat under the next table. The owner greets you at the door.

visit.brief: Get a table for two, ask what's fresh, and order a proper dinner with something to drink.
visit.summary: Dinner for two by the window: fish from the island, a Greek salad, bread and half a kilo of wine.
visit.translation:
— Good evening! How many people?
— Good evening. A table for two, please.
— Of course. Here, by the window.
— The menu, please. Do you have fish today?
— Yes, fresh fish from the island. And the Greek salad is very good.
— Lovely. A Greek salad, fish for two, and bread.
— And to drink? Wine, beer?
— Half a kilo of wine, please. And a bottle of water.
— Right away. Enjoy your meal!
— Thank you. Cheers!

bundle.gloss: One, three and four change with gender

prompts.situation: You walk into a taverna with a friend. Ask for a table for two.
Order a Greek salad, bread and wine.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Μια χωριάτικη, ψωμί και κρασί, παρακαλώ.

title: Στον δρόμο
brief: A hot afternoon in a town you don't know. You want the beach, and a cash machine on the way.

visit.brief: Stop someone, ask the way to the beach, and find out where there's a bank.
visit.summary: A passer-by sent you straight on and left for the beach, and pointed out a bank on the square by the pharmacy.
visit.translation:
— Excuse me! Where is the beach?
— The beach? Straight on, then on the left.
— Is it far?
— No, it's near here. Ten minutes.
— And where is there a bank?
— There's a bank on the square, next to the pharmacy.
— On the right or on the left?
— On the right, opposite the church.
— Thank you very much!
— Don't mention it. Have a good one!

bundle.gloss: σε + article = στο, στη, στον, στα

prompts.situation: Stop someone in the street and ask where the beach is.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Με συγχωρείτε, πού είναι η παραλία;

prompts.situation: A lost tourist asks you for the square. Tell them: straight on, then on the right.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Όλο ευθεία, και μετά στα δεξιά.

title: Στο λιμάνι
brief: The ticket window at the port of Piraeus. Ferries, gulls, a queue behind you.

visit.brief: Buy a return ticket to Naxos for tomorrow morning and find out when the boat leaves.
visit.summary: Bought a return ticket to Naxos for the 7:30 ferry tomorrow, paid by card, platform three.
visit.translation:
— Good morning. I'd like a ticket to Naxos.
— For today or for tomorrow?
— For tomorrow morning. What time does the boat leave?
— At half past seven. One way or return?
— Return, please. How much is it?
— Seventy euros. Card or cash?
— By card, please.
— Here's the ticket and the receipt. Platform three.
— Thank you. Have a good day!

bundle.gloss: The Greek question mark is a semicolon ;

prompts.situation: At the port ticket window: say you'd like a return ticket to Naxos for tomorrow morning.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Θα ήθελα ένα εισιτήριο για τη Νάξο, για αύριο το πρωί, με επιστροφή.

prompts.situation: Ask what time the ferry leaves.

title: Στο ξενοδοχείο
brief: Reception of a small hotel, late evening. A bell, a bowl of sweets, a tired receptionist who brightens up.

visit.brief: Check in: say you have a reservation, give your name, and find out about the room and breakfast.
visit.summary: Checked in for three nights; room on the third floor with a sea view, breakfast from seven to ten.
visit.dialogue:
— Καλησπέρα. Έχω κράτηση. Με λένε Μαρία Σμιθ.
— Καλώς ήρθατε! Ένα λεπτό… Ναι, ένα δωμάτιο για δύο άτομα, τρεις νύχτες.
— Σωστά. Έχει θέα στη θάλασσα;
— Ναι, στον τρίτο όροφο. Το διαβατήριό σας, παρακαλώ.
— Ορίστε.
— Ευχαριστώ. Το κλειδί σας. Το πρωινό είναι από τις επτά μέχρι τις δέκα.
— Υπάρχει ασανσέρ;
— Ναι, εκεί δεξιά. Καλή διαμονή!
— Ευχαριστώ πολύ. Καληνύχτα!
visit.translation:
— Good evening. I have a reservation. My name is Maria Smith.
— Welcome! One moment… Yes, a room for two people, three nights.
— That's right. Does it have a sea view?
— Yes, on the third floor. Your passport, please.
— Here you are.
— Thank you. Your key. Breakfast is from seven until ten.
— Is there a lift?
— Yes, over there on the right. Enjoy your stay!
— Thank you very much. Good night!

prompts.situation: At reception: say you have a reservation and give your name.
Ask whether the room has a sea view.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Έχει θέα στη θάλασσα το δωμάτιο;

title: Στο φαρμακείο
brief: Too much sun yesterday. A green cross, a cool shop, a pharmacist in a white coat.

visit.brief: Explain that your head hurts, understand how to take what you're given, and buy sunscreen.
visit.summary: Got pills for a headache from the sun, one morning and one evening with water, and a small sunscreen.
visit.translation:
— Good morning. I need help. It hurts here, my head.
— Do you have a fever?
— No, I don't think so. I'm a bit worn out from the sun.
— I see. Take these pills, one in the morning and one in the evening.
— Twice a day?
— Yes. With water, after food. Would you like sunscreen too?
— Yes, please. A small one.
— Here you are. Twelve euros.
— Thank you very much. Have a good day!

bundle.gloss: Not: δεν before the verb, μην for don't

prompts.situation: You have a headache. Tell the pharmacist it hurts here, pointing at your head.

title: Στη λαϊκή
brief: Saturday street market. Crates of tomatoes, a man shouting prices, melons the size of footballs.

visit.brief: Buy tomatoes and olives by the kilo, ask what things cost, and get your change.
visit.summary: Bought a kilo of tomatoes and half a kilo of olives from a stall holder who tried to sell a melon too.
visit.translation:
— Good morning! Fresh tomatoes, fresh melons! What would you like?
— Good morning. A kilo of tomatoes, please. How much are they?
— Two euros a kilo.
— And half a kilo of olives. Are they from here?
— Yes, from our village. Would you like a melon too? It's very sweet.
— No, thank you. That's all. How much is everything?
— Five euros.
— Here's ten.
— Your change. A bag?
— Yes, please. Thank you, have a good day!

prompts.situation: At the stall: ask for a kilo of tomatoes and half a kilo of olives.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Ένα κιλό ντομάτες και μισό κιλό ελιές, παρακαλώ.

title: Πινακίδες στην πόλη
brief: A walk through town with a Greek friend who has decided you're going to read every sign you pass.

visit.brief: Sound out the capitals on the signs around you: entrances, exits, the pharmacy, the toilets, and the one that says you can't go in.
visit.summary: Read a dozen signs out loud with a friend: ΕΙΣΟΔΟΣ, ΕΞΟΔΟΣ, ΦΑΡΜΑΚΕΙΟ, ΑΝΟΙΧΤΟ, ΤΟΥΑΛΕΤΕΣ, and ΑΠΑΓΟΡΕΥΕΤΑΙ Η ΕΙΣΟΔΟΣ.
visit.dialogue:
— Κοίτα, τι λέει εκεί; ΕΙΣΟΔΟΣ.
— Είσοδος, ναι. Και εδώ ΕΞΟΔΟΣ, η έξοδος.
— Και αυτό; ΦΑΡΜΑΚΕΙΟ;
— Φαρμακείο. Είναι ΑΝΟΙΧΤΟ, βλέπεις; Όχι ΚΛΕΙΣΤΟ.
— Ωραία. Και ΤΟΥΑΛΕΤΕΣ, αριστερά. ΑΝΔΡΩΝ και ΓΥΝΑΙΚΩΝ.
— Σωστά! Προσοχή τώρα: ΑΠΑΓΟΡΕΥΕΤΑΙ Η ΕΙΣΟΔΟΣ. Δεν πάμε από εδώ.
— Εντάξει. Και ΠΡΟΣ ΠΑΡΑΛΙΑ, δεξιά!
— Μπράβο. Διαβάζεις ελληνικά!
visit.translation:
— Look, what does it say there? ENTRANCE.
— Entrance, yes. And here EXIT, the exit.
— And this? PHARMACY?
— Pharmacy. It's OPEN, see? Not CLOSED.
— Nice. And TOILETS, on the left. MEN and WOMEN.
— Right! Careful now: NO ENTRY. We don't go this way.
— Okay. And TO THE BEACH, on the right!
— Well done. You're reading Greek!

bundle.gloss: Reading signs: capitals without accents, final sigma

prompts.situation: You see ΑΠΑΓΟΡΕΥΕΤΑΙ Η ΕΙΣΟΔΟΣ on a gate. Tell your friend what it says and that you won't go that way.
prompts.exampleAnswer: Απαγορεύεται η είσοδος. Δεν πάμε από εδώ.

prompts.situation: Your friend points at a door marked ΕΞΟΔΟΣ and asks what it is. Answer.
